findings.issue: The edge case 'hand write still running when Leave is chosen' (spec section 7) relies on SPEC-07/SPEC-09, but neither test makes the write pending when Leave is clicked. leaveAfterHand1 clicks Leave once 'Hand over' is visible. By then the worker grade and the IndexedDB add have usually finished (they run in real time; the paused clock does not hold them). If the tableWritesSettled() wait in App.leave were removed, these tests would most likely still pass.
findings.evidence: App.tsx leave: tableWritesSettled().then(() => sharedHandStore().endSession(...)). No e2e or unit test delays the grade or the hand write. App has no unit tests (no jsdom).
findings.fix: Make the write pending on purpose in one e2e. For example, use page.route on the advice worker script to hold its first grade reply (or wrap indexedDB in an init script so the hands 'add' is held) until after the Leave click. Then assert the report shows '1 hand' and the stored session has handsPlayed 1. Otherwise, note in the spec that this ordering is only covered by chance.

findings.issue: leave() calls tableWritesSettled() inside the click handler. useTableSession only starts tracking the last hand's write in a passive effect (the step === 'done' branch). If Leave is clicked after the hand-over commit but before React flushes that effect, the write starts after the chain has been captured. endSession could then run before the hand write, and the late handWrite put would replace the session record without endedAt. The result would be an ended report plus a resumable session, or a 0-hand delete followed by a re-created session. The window is a few milliseconds and needs Leave mid-hand at the exact moment the hand completes, so this is unlikely in practice.
findings.evidence: useTableSession.ts: track(write.current) runs in useEffect after the 'done' render. App.tsx leave: tableWritesSettled() is called synchronously in the handler, before React re-renders and unmounts the Table.
findings.fix: Capture the chain after React has committed the unmount, which flushes pending passive effects. For example, call tableWritesSettled() from a setTimeout(0) or from an effect of the 'ending' screen instead of synchronously in the handler. Or leave a comment that documents the accepted window.

findings.issue: object/whole/isoString/invalid are a fourth copy of the private validators already in hand-record.ts (object, whole, invalid) and session-record.ts (object, whole, isoString, invalid). The only difference is the error-message prefix.
findings.evidence: src/table/session-record.ts:139-155 and src/table/hand-record.ts:147,258,272 define the same helpers.
findings.fix: This follows the existing per-module pattern, so it is acceptable for this slice. Optionally, a later refactor could extract a shared validator factory that takes the prefix (out of scope here).

findings.issue: SPEC-10 says hand 215/101 is not stored. The test checks storedRecords right after the report shows, without advancing the clock. A late write would therefore not be seen.
findings.evidence: expect(await storedRecords(page)).toEqual([]) follows directly after the tile check, with no page.clock.runFor.
findings.fix: Add await page.clock.runFor(5000) before the storedRecords/storedSessions checks, as SPEC-07/09 do.

summary: The implementation matches the spec. DB v3 only adds the 'reports' store through an appended oldVersion < 3 step. The SPEC-12 test seeds a real v2 database and checks byte-identical records and the store list. endSession runs entirely inside the request callbacks of one strict transaction over sessions+reports. Its put and add happen together. A duplicate add aborts the transaction, which also rolls back the endedAt put, and SPEC-04 asserts session A's JSON is unchanged, so a split transaction would be caught. A 0-hand session is deleted and resolves null. A corrupt record aborts with the parse error. bbPer100 matches the spec's integer half-away-from-zero formula and never returns -0. All worked-example rows are asserted, and parse rejects a 0.1 drift. App.leave guards a double call, steps off history, shows the busy 'ending' screen, waits for tableWritesSettled and handles null and rejection as A-5 says. The five locked e2e edits replace only the pause-to-Home expectations. The draw-count, deal-nothing-more ([13]/[1]) and no-table checks stay, and stronger report, endedAt and focus assertions are added. The two unlocked unit edits change only version literals to DB_VERSION / DB_VERSION + 1 and add REPORTS_STORE; no assertion is removed. Main gap: no test makes the hand write pending when Leave is clicked, so the tableWritesSettled wait is only covered by chance (MINOR). There is also a small React effect-timing window in leave (MINOR). There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
